ต้องการสร้างเว็บไซต์เป็นรูปแบบหน้าปฏิทิน เพื่อเก็บประวัติการลาเป็นในรูปแบบปฏิทิน โดยการลาจะแยกสีการลาแต่ละประเภท
1. ประเภทการลาจะแบ่งออกเป็น ลากิจส่วนตัว, ลาป่วย, ลาพักผ่อน, ลาคลอดบุตร, ลาอุปสมบท
2. เมื่อเข้าเว็บไซต์ให้เจอหน้าแรก แยกปุ่มเป็น 3 หน่วยงาน เวชระเบียนผู้ป่วยนอก, เวชระเบียนผู้ป่วยใน, ศูนย์ข้อมูล
3. เมื่อคลิกของหน่วยงานใดไป ให้เจอหน้าปฏิทินการลา และมีช่องให้พิมพ์ค้นหารายชื่อคนที่ต้องการจะลา(ขึ้นข้อความอัตโนมัติเมื่อพิมพ์ต่ออักษรย่อ) และเด้งรายชื่อให้เลือก เลือกวันที่จะลา(ดีไซต์ให้ง่ายต่อผู้ใช้งานที่สุด) และมีกราฟหรือจำนวนวันลาให้ดูได้ว่าในช่วง มกราคม - พฤษภาคม , มิถุนายน - ธันวาคม มีการลาไปกี่วันแล้ว

**Conceptualizing The Interface**

I'm currently focused on the core view – a calendar interface. I'm visualizing how to integrate color-coded leave types for easy identification. The application's goal, a leave management system, is clearly defined, and the calendar is the central point. I'm exploring the visual aspects of this calendar display.


**Defining Department Views**

I've outlined specific department views, starting from a landing page with department selection. Within each department, I'll incorporate a searchable user list and intuitive date selection. The core calendar visualization remains central, with added statistical analysis displayed via Recharts graphs, focusing on leave counts by periods. Date-fns will be essential, but it's important to remember to favor standard libraries.


**Evaluating Date Libraries**

I'm currently evaluating the use of a lightweight helper library or the native `Date` object for calendar implementation. Though the task description highlights using popular libraries, the preference is to stick with native `Date/Intl` where possible for the sake of simplicity. I may also implement a custom, dependency-light calendar logic.


**Prioritizing UI/UX Focus**

I've decided to prioritize the UI/UX functionality initially, using `faker` or static lists for data generation if needed. I'm intentionally not forcing the Gemini API into the core flow unless it adds demonstrable value, though I'll include a "Leave Insight AI" button to satisfy that particular prompt.

I've also decided to use `localStorage` for data persistence since there is no backend specified, so users can switch departments and add leaves. The global state will need to track `currentDepartment`, `employees` and `leaves`. I will also break down the code into components.


**Defining Component Architecture**

I'm currently structuring my components into specific, logical files: `LeaveCalendar.tsx` will house the calendar grid, `LeaveForm.tsx` handles the leave addition, and `StatsPanel.tsx` displays the charts. I'm also planning to implement predefined color codes for different leave types such as personal (blue), sick (red), vacation (green), maternity (pink), and ordination (orange/yellow).


**Developing Functional Components**

I'm currently fleshing out the application's core. I've broken down components further: `LeaveCalendar.tsx`, `StatsChart.tsx`, and `App.tsx` are now clearly defined. I'm also drafting the Thai name mock list for the search functionality. I am now working on an "Ask AI about Leave Policy" button, which I'll use to integrate the Gemini API per the instructions.


**Implementing Leave Entry**

I've decided to implement a modal form for leave entry on date clicks or through an "Add Leave" button. I'll use Recharts to display a bar chart comparing the two requested periods: Jan-May and Jun-Dec. I've broken down the files into `metadata.json`, `index.html`, `index.tsx`, `types.ts`, `constants.ts`, and a `services` folder, where I will integrate the logic. I am grouping data accordingly for chart generation.


**Assembling The Pieces**

I'm now integrating the Gemini API, particularly focusing on how to summarize leave data using `@google/genai`. I'm configuring the AI model with the `gemini-3-flash-preview` for text processing. I'm also preparing for the UI layout with a 3-card landing page and the main application view with a sidebar for user search and statistics. I'll focus on the data model to get the `geminiService.ts` function working with the chart and calendar.

**Considering Redesign Options**

I'm currently focused on the calendar layout redesign. I'm exploring adjustments to the proportions of the Search, Annual Stats, and Calendar sections to improve visual appeal and usability. I've also decided to implement a new font across the entire system. I'm thinking about Kanit.


**Implementing Aesthetic Updates**

I've been analyzing the current UI's layout, noting the CSS Grid structure, Tailwind slate color scheme, and Sarabun font. It's functional but lacks visual flair. I plan to introduce Kanit as the global font, updating the HTML and Tailwind config files. Furthermore, I intend to redesign the layout, moving the Search bar to the top of the content area for better space utilization, instead of the 4/8 split.


**Refining Layout & Styling**

I'm now zeroing in on a cleaner layout strategy. The plan is to create a two-column setup. One column will house the profile card or search box and stats chart. The other will be the calendar. I'm exploring different column widths, either a 3/12 or 4/12 split for the left, and 9/12 or 8/12 for the right. I'm focused on card designs with softer shadows and better padding for styling, and I will be refining the components' styling, specifically the calendar grid gaps, search box's distinction, and ensuring the stats chart fits well. Also, I am checking the Thai year format.


**Analyzing Component Changes**

My current focus is on the specific components. I'm updating `index.html` to use Kanit, as well as refreshing the `App.tsx` grid layout, considering the best place for the search bar, either a top bar or side-by-side. I'm also planning softer backgrounds. Within `CalendarView.tsx`, I want to improve the legibility of the calendar numbers and chip styling for leave types. Finally, I'll adjust `StatsChart.tsx` to align with the new Kanit aesthetic.


**Structuring the Layout**

I'm now zeroing in on the layout structure using a card-based UI. The focus is on a sidebar and main content area. The sidebar will contain the user profile, stats chart and the AI analysis action buttons, while the main content area will house the calendar, following the updated Kanit font implementation in both `index.html` and `App.tsx`. I'll be adjusting calendar visuals by removing heavy borders and introducing gaps, shadows or subtle borders for a cleaner look.


**Improving Visual Structure**

I'm now prioritizing the visual structure, aiming for a cleaner and more readable design. I'm focusing on incorporating ample whitespace and clear headings throughout. I intend to use `rounded-2xl` on the main container and `min-h-[120px]` for calendar cells to optimize space. I'll also check `StatsChart.tsx` for any necessary minor style adjustments. Specifically, in `App.tsx`, I'll rework the layout, experimenting with column ratios like 4/8 or 3.5/8.5 to balance the sidebar (search & stats) with the calendar, ensuring the chart remains easily readable.


**Updating Specific Components**

Now, I'm focusing on the code-level changes. In `index.html`, I've verified the Kanit font inclusion, and I've started wrapping the search and stats elements in an `<aside>` tag within `App.tsx` and calendar element with a `<section>` tag. I'm exploring cleaner search input styles, and the possibility of a "Summary Card" is intriguing. Finally, I will clean up calendar grid borders in `CalendarView.tsx` and adjust the stats chart's title with dynamic year computation.


**Generating XML Structures**

I'm now generating XML structures based on my layout decisions. I've re-reviewed the Thai year format. I'll stick with the `currentYear + 543` calculation. I will start the XML structure generation using steps detailed from my notes. I'm focusing on updating the `index.html`, `App.tsx`, `CalendarView.tsx`, and `StatsChart.tsx` files. Specifically, I'm integrating the Kanit font, redesigning the layout with a sidebar (search, profile, stats) and main content (calendar) structure, modernizing calendar headers, softening day cells, and styling the stats chart.

To satisfy your request to redesign the application with a focus on the calendar layout, staff search, annual statistics, and changing the font to "Kanit", I will update the following files.

Here is the specification of changes:
1.  **Font**: Update `index.html` to import the **Kanit** font family from Google Fonts and configure Tailwind to use it as the default sans-serif font.
2.  **Layout (App.tsx)**:
    *   Refactor the main grid layout to a **3:9 ratio** (Sidebar : Calendar) on large screens to give the calendar more breathing room while keeping the tools accessible.
    *   **Sidebar**: Redesign the Search box to be cleaner. Group the "Employee Profile" and "Statistics" into a cohesive vertical dashboard.
    *   **Aesthetics**: Use softer shadows (`shadow-lg`, `shadow-xl`), rounded corners (`rounded-2xl`), and a cleaner color palette.
3.  **Calendar (CalendarView.tsx)**:
    *   Modernize the header with better navigation buttons.
    *   Improve day cells: Remove harsh borders, use subtle backgrounds, and styling for "Today".
    *   Make leave indicators clearer.
4.  **Statistics (StatsChart.tsx)**:
    *   Update the chart container to blend with the new design.
    *   Ensure the Thai year (e.g., 2569) is displayed prominently.

2.  **Google Apps Script (Backend) ยังไม่อัปเดต:** โค้ดฝั่ง Google Apps Script ต้องถูกแก้ไขให้ส่งข้อมูล "รายการวันลา" กลับมาด้วย (จากเดิมส่งแค่รายชื่อ) และต้องกด **Deploy ใหม่**

1.  **คัดลอกโค้ด `google-apps-script.js` ด้านล่าง** ไปวางทับใน Google Apps Script Editor
2.  **กด Deploy -> New deployment** (เลือก Web app, ใครมีสิทธิ์เข้าถึง: ทุกคน)
3.  **นำ URL ใหม่** มาใส่ใน `App.tsx` (ถ้า URL เปลี่ยน) หรือถ้า URL เดิมก็ใช้ได้เลย

*   **App.tsx:** เพิ่ม `?t=${new Date().getTime()}` ต่อท้าย URL ตอนดึงข้อมูล เพื่อบังคับให้ระบบดึงข้อมูลล่าสุดเสมอ (แก้ปัญหา Cache) และเพิ่มการแจ้งเตือนถ้าพบว่า Apps Script ยังเป็นเวอร์ชันเก่า
*   **google-apps-script.js:** ปรับปรุงฟังก์ชัน `doGet` ให้ส่งข้อมูลวันที่ลา (leaves) กลับมาให้หน้าเว็บ

กำหนดวันหยุดนักขัตฤกษ์ปี 2569 (2026): ระบุวันสำคัญทางศาสนาตามปฏิทินจันทรคติ และวันหยุดชดเชยกรณีตรงกับเสาร์-อาทิตย์ ให้ถูกต้องแม่นยำ

I've just finished analyzing the user's initial request. I've updated the `constants.ts` file to properly exclude Labor Day and Teachers' Day for the 2026 holiday calendar, conforming to government and Thai calendar regulations. This sets a solid foundation for further development.


**Analyzing User Concerns**

I'm now focusing on the user's specific concern about booking leave on non-government holidays like Labor Day. I need to figure out why the system might be preventing leave booking on these days. It appears the logic currently is too strict, or that some UI functionality is malfunctioning. The user wants to book on any day that isn't a government holiday or a holiday connected to the Ministry of Public Health.


**Investigating Booking Restrictions**

I'm now examining the `App.tsx` file, specifically the `handleDateClick` function. The logic currently blocks date selection if the day is a weekend or a holiday, determined by `getHolidayName`. This is where the issue lies: `getHolidayName` is returning a value for Labor Day (May 1st) after I removed it from `FIXED_HOLIDAYS`, indicating a problem in the holiday determination process. I need to identify why a null value isn't being properly evaluated as a non-holiday.


**Examining Conditional Logic**

I'm now zeroing in on the conditional logic within `App.tsx`, specifically the `calculatedDatesToAdd` section. My current line of thinking revolves around the `isHoliday` check. Initially, removing Labor Day from the `constants.ts` file should have allowed booking on that day, as `getHolidayName` would return null, making `isHoliday` false. I'm now testing this hypothesis, confirming that `!isHoliday` should evaluate to true when Labor Day is selected after it has been removed from the holiday constant array.


**Revisiting Holiday Logic**

I'm revisiting `getHolidayName` function in `constants.ts` because the user wants to ensure non-government holidays are bookable in 2026 and *future* years. My hypothesis is that the initial `constants.ts` change may have been incomplete, possibly only affecting 2026 specifically. I'm double-checking the logic to make sure the function correctly handles future years based on the Thai calendar and correctly identifies and excludes non-government holidays like Labor Day from the booking restrictions.


**Refining Holiday Calculations**

I'm now zeroing in on the holiday calculation logic, specifically addressing the user's need for future year holiday support, not just 2026. My current code uses a fallback to `FIXED_HOLIDAYS` for years beyond 2026, which incorrectly excludes lunar holidays like Visakha Bucha. I'm modifying the code to account for and calculate lunar holidays in future years based on the Thai calendar to properly reflect which dates are non-work days. This should resolve the underlying issue.


**Clarifying Year-Specific Holidays**

My current focus is on the user's issue with booking non-government holidays in future years. I've realized the logic might be misinterpreting the user's need. I'm examining how future years beyond 2026 are being handled. My initial changes may not have fully addressed the need to differentiate between government holidays and user-defined "non-holidays" across different years. I need to make sure the user can book leave on a day like Labor Day in *any* year, not just 2026.



**Interpreting User Requirements**

I'm now clarifying the user's intent. It seems I might have misinterpreted the request. The user is asking to adjust the holiday logic for 2026 and future years to allow booking on days like Labor Day, which isn't a government holiday, and that this logic must be maintained in the future. I need to make sure I am handling future years robustly. I'm focusing on the Thai calendar and its implications.


**Analyzing Holiday Handling**

I'm now focusing on how the weekend and fixed holiday logic interact. I've realized the user *may* want to book on weekends under certain shift circumstances. I'm reevaluating the holiday determination process and ensuring it correctly handles weekend selection, while still excluding fixed holidays. It looks like the user's issue with Labor Day might be due to a misunderstanding of how the weekend and holiday exclusions are applied. I need to make sure weekend selection is only excluded when *not* working a shift, and I need to review what "fixed holidays" means with respect to weekend/non-weekend.


**Expanding Year Coverage**

I'm now expanding the hardcoded logic to cover more years, as the user desires. I'm updating `constants.ts` to include holiday definitions for 2025, 2026, and 2027. I'll need to update `getHolidayName` to select the proper holiday list based on the year to ensure accuracy. I'll maintain a clean `FIXED_HOLIDAYS` list, and add the new year constants. This addresses the need for forward year support, but I must also consider the edge cases of these years.


**Revisiting Year Selection**

I'm now tracing the year selection logic. It seems I accidentally overwrote holiday data for the current year, 2025, with that for 2026. This would make the holidays in 2025 incomplete, which may be the current source of user confusion. I need to make sure the calendar correctly displays holidays for the current year. I will address any calendar discrepancies by fixing the incorrect value assignments.



**Updating Holiday Definitions**

I'm now integrating the updated holiday definitions for 2025, 2026, and 2027 into `constants.ts`. The changes will correctly exclude weekends and holidays, while allowing leave bookings on non-government holidays like Labor Day. I've updated the logic to include 2025 (current year), ensuring accurate holiday representation, and removing the erroneous Labor Day data that caused calendar inaccuracies.


**Defining Future Holidays**

I'm now integrating holidays for 2027 into `constants.ts`, including Makha Bucha (2/22), Visakha Bucha (5/20), Asarnha Bucha (7/17), and Buddhist Lent. **Clarifying Holiday Rules**

I'm now clarifying the user's intent concerning weekend booking and the distinction between government and non-government holidays. It looks like the user wants Labor Day and Teachers' Day to be bookable, while government holidays and weekends are blocked unless working a shift. The user may be simulating the user interaction. I'm focusing on ensuring Labor Day is bookable and weekends are correctly excluded under standard leave-counting circumstances.


**Refining Holiday Definitions**

I'm now refining the `constants.ts` file. I am working on the comprehensive holiday lists. I've removed Labor Day from `FIXED_HOLIDAYS`, and will add it to the yearly holiday definitions. I am separating holiday definitions into year-specific constants: `HOLIDAYS_2025`, `HOLIDAYS_2026`, `HOLIDAYS_2027` to make the data clearer. I'm verifying that the holiday exclusions work correctly for each listed year, and that weekends are blocked unless specifically requested.


**Verifying Holiday Exclusion**

I'm now integrating holidays for 2027, as well as holidays for 2025. I am making sure that government holidays and weekend selection are correctly excluded, while leaving non-government holidays such as Labor Day, bookable. I will ensure that the holiday exclusions work correctly for each listed year, and address any potential overlap.



**Integrating Future Holidays**

I'm now integrating the provided 2026 and 2027 holiday data into the `constants.ts` file, creating `HOLIDAYS_2026` and `HOLIDAYS_2027` objects. I've integrated fixed holidays to each of these objects. I'm taking care to correctly handle any potential overlapping dates, and will make sure Labor Day is excluded for booking.


**Implementing Holiday Adjustments**

I'm now implementing the 2027 holiday data, adding it to `constants.ts` with corresponding objects. I'm taking care to correctly implement the listed dates, including substitute holidays, and ensuring that Labor Day (May 1st) remains bookable. I'm verifying that the structure is consistent and robust enough for future year expansions.


**Enabling Weekend Selection**

I'm now focusing on how weekends are handled within the date selection logic, and I am re-evaluating whether the current behavior aligns with the user's intent. The prompt highlights a need for flexibility regarding weekend selection, especially with the user's request, implying they want the blocking logic to be customizable, such as configuring weekends. I need to make sure the "fixed holidays" also comply to this rule.

-- 🔴 คำสั่งซ่อมแซมความสัมพันธ์ตาราง (Foreign Key)
-- ช่วยแก้ปัญหาและป้องกันข้อมูลขยะ (Orphan Data)
-- ให้ Copy โค้ดนี้ไปรันใน SQL Editor แล้วกด Run

-- 1. ลบ Constraint เก่าออกก่อน (ถ้ามี)
ALTER TABLE leaves DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS leaves_employee_id_fkey;

-- 2. สร้าง Constraint ใหม่ โดยกำหนดให้ "ลบข้อมูลแบบลูกโซ่" (ON DELETE CASCADE)
-- แปลว่า: ถ้าลบรายชื่อพนักงาน ข้อมูลการลาของคนนั้นจะหายไปโดยอัตโนมัติ ไม่ค้างในระบบ
ALTER TABLE leaves
  ADD CONSTRAINT leaves_employee_id_fkey
  FOREIGN KEY (employee_id)
  REFERENCES employees(id)
  ON DELETE CASCADE;

-- 3. ตรวจสอบและลบข้อมูลขยะ (วันลาที่ไม่มีเจ้าของ) ที่อาจตกค้างอยู่
DELETE FROM leaves
WHERE employee_id NOT IN (SELECT id FROM employees);
